325:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
326:     pub(crate) fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
327:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
328:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
329:         let has_opener = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
330:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
331: 
332:         if has_opener && !has_end {
333:             return true;
334:         }
335: 
336:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
337:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
338:             let kind = prev.kind();
339:             if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&kind) {
340:                 return true;
341:             }
342:         }
343: 
344:         false
345:     }
346: 
347:     /// the call.
348:     pub(crate) fn is_in_function_call_args(node: &Node) -> bool {
349:         let mut current = node.parent();
350:         while let Some(ancestor) = current {
351:             match ancestor.kind() {
352:                 "arguments" => {
353:                     return ancestor
354:                         .parent()
355:                         .is_some_and(|p| p.kind() == "function_call");
356:                 }
357:                 "function_call" => {
358:                     // The ERROR is a direct child of the call. It is within the
359:                     // argument list when the call also has an `arguments` child.
360:                     let mut cursor = ancestor.walk();
361:                     return ancestor
362:                         .children(&mut cursor)
363:                         .any(|c| c.kind() == "arguments");
364:                 }
365:                 _ => {}
366:             }
367:             current = ancestor.parent();
368:         }
369:         false
370:     }
371: 
372:     /// that starts with a block-opening keyword).
373:     pub(crate) fn classify_missing_end(
374:         node: &Node,
375:         source: &str,
376:     ) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
377:         let start = node.start_byte();
378:         let node_end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
379:         let text = &source[start..node_end];
380:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
381:         let line = node.start_position().row + 1;
382: 
383:         // ENDCT4: ERROR text contains "classdef", a function_definition
384:         // follows it as a sibling, and no "methods" appears between them.
385:         if lower.contains("classdef") {
386:             let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
387:             while let Some(sib) = sibling {
388:                 if sib.kind() == "function_definition" && sib.start_byte() > start {
389:                     let between = &source[node_end..sib.start_byte()];
390:                     if !between.to_lowercase().contains("methods") {
391:                         return Some((
392:                             "ENDCT4",
393:                             "A METHODS block or END might be missing before the function definition. This might be causing additional error messages.".to_string(),
394:                         ));
395:                     }
396:                     break;
397:                 }
398:                 sibling = sib.next_sibling();
399:             }
400:         }
401: 
402:         // ENDCT2: a block opener appears in the ERROR text or its previous
403:         // sibling, and the ERROR does not contain `end`.
404:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
405:         if !has_end {
406:             let opener_in_text = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
407:             let opener_in_prev = node
408:                 .prev_sibling()
409:                 .map(|prev| {
410:                     let prev_text = &source[prev.start_byte()..prev.end_byte()];
411:                     BLOCK_OPENERS
412:                         .iter()
413:                         .any(|kw| prev_text.to_lowercase().contains(kw))
414:                 })
415:                 .unwrap_or(false);
416:             if opener_in_text || opener_in_prev {
417:                 let raw_end = node.end_position().row;
418:                 let end_line = if source[..node_end].ends_with('\n') {
419:                     raw_end
420:                 } else {
421:                     raw_end + 1
422:                 };
423:                 let opener_line = if opener_in_text {
424:                     line
425:                 } else {
426:                     node.prev_sibling()
427:                         .map(|p| p.start_position().row + 1)
428:                         .unwrap_or(line)
429:                 };
430:                 return Some((
431:                     "ENDCT2",
432:                     format!(
433:                         "An END might be missing (after line {end_line}), possibly matching line {opener_line}."
434:                     ),
435:                 ));
436:             }
437:         }
438: 
439:         // ENDCT3: the ERROR is followed by a sibling that starts with a
440:         // block-opening keyword.
441:         let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
442:         while let Some(sib) = sibling {
443:             let sib_text = &source[sib.start_byte()..sib.end_byte()];
444:             match sib_text.split_whitespace().next() {
445:                 Some(first) if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&first.to_lowercase().as_str()) => {
446:                     let kw = text.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_uppercase();
447:                     let matched = first.to_uppercase();
448:                     return Some((
449:                         "ENDCT3",
450:                         format!(
451:                             "An END might be missing (before {kw} on line {line}), possibly matching {matched}."
452:                         ),
453:                     ));
454:                 }
455:                 Some(_) => break,
456:                 None => {}
457:             }
458:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
459:         }
460: 
461:         None
462:     }

485:     /// Returns the first reserved keyword appearing as a whole word in `text`.
486:     pub(crate) fn contains_reserved_word(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
487:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
488:         RESERVED_KEYWORDS
489:             .iter()

491:             .copied()

494:     /// Whole-word substring check: `needle` must not be part of a larger word.
495:     pub(crate) fn contains_whole_word(haystack: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {
496:         let mut search_start = 0;
497:         while let Some(rel) = haystack[search_start..].find(needle) {
498:             let idx = search_start + rel;
499:             let prev = haystack[..idx].chars().next_back();
500:             let next = haystack[idx + needle.len()..].chars().next();
501:             let left_ok = prev.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
502:             let right_ok = next.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
503:             if left_ok && right_ok {
504:                 return true;
505:             }
506:             search_start = idx + needle.len();
507:         }
508:         false
509:     }

597:     /// Collect all `number` nodes and all ERROR nodes in document order.

626:     /// Parse a hex or binary literal into (is_hex, digit count, type suffix).
627:     pub(crate) fn parse_hex_binary_literal(text: &str) -> Option<(bool, usize, Option<&str>)> {
628:         let (is_hex, rest) = if text.starts_with("0x") || text.starts_with("0X") {
629:             (true, &text[2..])
630:         } else if text.starts_with("0b") || text.starts_with("0B") {
631:             (false, &text[2..])
632:         } else {
633:             return None;
634:         };
635: 
636:         if rest.is_empty() {
637:             return None;
638:         }
639: 
640:         let suffix = if rest.len() >= 3 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 3..]).is_some() {
641:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 3..])
642:         } else if rest.len() >= 2 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 2..]).is_some() {
643:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 2..])
644:         } else {
645:             None
646:         };
647: 
648:         let digits = match suffix {
649:             Some(s) => &rest[..rest.len() - s.len()],
650:             None => rest,
651:         };
652: 
653:         if digits.is_empty() {
654:             return None;
655:         }
656: 
657:         Some((is_hex, digits.chars().count(), suffix))
658:     }
659: 
660:     /// Bit width for a valid type suffix (`u8`/`s8` ... `u64`/`s64`), or None.
661:     pub(crate) fn suffix_bits(suffix: &str) -> Option<usize> {
662:         if suffix.len() < 2 {
663:             return None;
664:         }
665:         let kind = suffix.as_bytes()[0];
666:         let is_valid_kind = kind == b'u' || kind == b'U' || kind == b's' || kind == b'S';
667:         if !is_valid_kind {
668:             return None;
669:         }
670:         match &suffix[1..] {
671:             "8" => Some(8),
672:             "16" => Some(16),
673:             "32" => Some(32),
674:             "64" => Some(64),
675:             _ => None,
676:         }
677:     }
678: 
679:     /// Maximum number of digits a type suffix allows for a literal.
680:     pub(crate) fn max_digits_for_suffix(suffix: &str, is_hex: bool) -> Option<usize> {
681:         let bits = Self::suffix_bits(suffix)?;
682:         if is_hex {
683:             Some(bits / 4)
684:         } else {
685:             Some(bits)
686:         }
687:     }

711:     pub(crate) fn push_name_value_diagnostic(
712:         &self,
713:         name: Node,
714:         source: &str,
715:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
716:     ) {
717:         // A valid MATLAB identifier is a legitimate name=value name.
718:         if name.kind() == "identifier" {
719:             return;
720:         }
721:         let is_string = name.kind() == "string" || Self::has_string_child(name);
722:         let check_id = if is_string { "FVACS" } else { "FVAMI" };
723:         if !self.is_check_enabled(check_id) {
724:             return;
725:         }
726:         let name_text = &source[name.start_byte()..name.end_byte()];
727:         let pos = name.start_position();
728:         let message = if is_string {
729:             "Using a character vector or string as a name in name=value syntax is not supported. Remove the quotes around the name."
730:         } else {
731:             "Name in name-value argument syntax must be a valid MATLAB identifier."
732:         };
733:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
734:             rule_id: check_id,
735:             message: format!("{message} (near '{name_text}')"),
736:             severity: Severity::Error,
737:             byte_range: name.byte_range(),
738:             line: pos.row + 1,
739:             column: pos.column + 1,
740:             fix: None,
741:         });
742:     }

3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_file_name(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8: 
9:         if !self.is_check_enabled("BDFIL") {
10:             return diagnostics;
11:         }
12: 
13:         if let Some(stem) = ctx.file_path.file_stem() {
14:             let name = stem.to_string_lossy();
15: 
16:             let valid = !name.is_empty()
17:                 && name.len() <= 63
18:                 && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
19:                 && name.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_');
20: 
21:             if !valid {
22:                 let reason = if name.is_empty() {
23:                     "file name is empty".to_string()
24:                 } else if name.len() > 63 {
25:                     format!("file name exceeds 63 characters ({} chars)", name.len())
26:                 } else if !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {
27:                     "file name must start with a letter".to_string()
28:                 } else {
29:                     "file name contains invalid characters (only alphanumeric and underscore allowed)".to_string()
30:                 };
31:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
32:                     rule_id: "BDFIL",
33:                     message: format!("Invalid MATLAB file name '{}': {}", name, reason),
34:                     severity: Severity::Error,
35:                     byte_range: 0..ctx.source.len().min(1),
36:                     line: 1,
37:                     column: 1,
38:                     fix: None,
39:                 });
40:             }
41:         }

44:     }

1: //! `check_assignment_lhs` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_assignment_lhs(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         self.walk_assignment_lhs(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
9:         diagnostics
10:     }
11: 
12:     pub(crate) fn walk_assignment_lhs(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         const OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS: [&str; 5] = [
19:             "comparison_operator",
20:             "binary_operator",
21:             "boolean_operator",
22:             "unary_operator",
23:             "postfix_operator",
24:         ];
25: 
26:         let kind = node.kind();
27: 
28:         if kind == "assignment" {
29:             let lhs = node.child_by_field_name("left");
30:             if let Some(lhs) = lhs {
31:                 let pos = lhs.start_position();
32: 
33:                 // UNSET: operator expression on the left side of `=`.
34:                 if self.is_check_enabled("UNSET") && OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS.contains(&lhs.kind()) {
35:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
36:                         rule_id: "UNSET",
37:                         message: "Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment"
38:                             .to_string(),
39:                         severity: Severity::Error,
40:                         byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
41:                         line: pos.row + 1,
42:                         column: pos.column + 1,
43:                         fix: None,
44:                     });
45:                 }
46: 
47:                 // LHROW: multi-output LHS containing a row separator (`;`).
48:                 if self.is_check_enabled("LHROW") && lhs.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
49:                     let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
50:                     if lhs_text.contains(';') {
51:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
52:                             rule_id: "LHROW",
53:                             message:
54:                                 "The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows (';')"
55:                                     .to_string(),
56:                             severity: Severity::Error,
57:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
58:                             line: pos.row + 1,
59:                             column: pos.column + 1,
60:                             fix: None,
61:                         });
62:                     }
63:                 }
64:             }
65:         }
66:

71:                         i += ch_len;
72:                         continue;
73:                     }
74:                 }
75:             }
76: 
77:             // BADNE: `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`).
78:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNE")
79:                 && b == b'!'
80:                 && i + 1 < len
81:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'='
82:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
83:             {
84:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
85:                     rule_id: "BADNE",
86:                     message: "Use '~=' instead of '!=' for not-equal in MATLAB".to_string(),
87:                     severity: Severity::Error,
88:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
89:                     line,
90:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
91:                     fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::new(i..i + 2, "~=")),
92:                 });
93:                 i += 2;
94:                 continue;
95:             }
96: 
97:             // BADOT: `..` not part of `...` (line continuation).
98:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADOT")
99:                 && b == b'.'
100:                 && i + 1 < len
101:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'.'
102:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
103:             {
104:                 // Check if this is part of `...` (line continuation).
105:                 let is_ellipsis = i + 2 < len && bytes[i + 2] == b'.';
106:                 if !is_ellipsis {
107:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
108:                         rule_id: "BADOT",
109:                         message: "Invalid '..' operator; did you mean '...' (line continuation)?"
110:                             .to_string(),
111:                         severity: Severity::Error,
112:                         byte_range: i..i + 2,
113:                         line,
114:                         column: i - line_start + 1,
115:                         fix: None,
116:                     });
117:                     i += 2;
118:                     continue;
119:                 } else {
120:                     // Skip the whole `...`.
121:                     i += 3;
122:                     continue;
123:                 }
124:             }
125: 
126:             // TWOCM: `,,` (double comma).
127:             if self.is_check_enabled("TWOCM")
128:                 && b == b','
129:                 && i + 1 < len
130:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b','
131:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
132:             {
133:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
134:                     rule_id: "TWOCM",
135:                     message: "Double comma ',,'; possible typo".to_string(),
136:                     severity: Severity::Error,
137:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
138:                     line,
139:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
140:                     fix: None,
141:                 });
142:                 i += 2;
143:                 continue;
144:             }
145: 
146:             // Advance past multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
147:             if b > 0x7F {
148:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
149:                     i += ch.len_utf8();
150:                     continue;
151:                 }
152:             }
153: 
154:             i += 1;
155:         }
156: 
157:         diagnostics

6:     pub(crate) fn check_file_structure(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         let mut cursor = root.walk();
9: 
10:         let mut class_count = 0usize;
11:         let mut has_non_class_statements = false;
12:         let mut has_function_def = false;
13:         let mut has_any_real_content = false;
14: 
15:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
16:             let kind = child.kind();
17:             match kind {
18:                 "class_definition" => class_count += 1,
19:                 "function_definition" => {
20:                     has_function_def = true;
21:                     has_any_real_content = true;
22:                 }
23:                 "comment" => {} // Comments don't count as content.
24:                 "expression_statement" => {
25:                     // Check if it's just a semicolon.
26:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
27:                     let trimmed = text.trim();
28:                     if trimmed == ";" {
29:                         // Empty statement — doesn't count as real content.
30:                     } else {

32:                         has_any_real_content = true;
33:                     }
34:                 }
35:                 _ if !child.is_error() && kind != "\n" => {
36:                     has_non_class_statements = true;
37:                     has_any_real_content = true;
38:                 }
39:                 _ => {}
40:             }
41:         }
42: 
43:         // CLTWO: Multiple class definitions in one file.
44:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLTWO") && class_count > 1 {

49:                 ),

52:                 line: 1,
53:                 column: 1,
54:                 fix: None,

56:         }
57:

73:             });
74:         }

78:             && class_count > 0

80:             && has_function_def

82:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {

91:             });
92:         }

97:             && class_count == 0
98:             && !source.trim().is_empty()

12:     pub(crate) fn walk_function_names(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:         in_methods_block: bool,
18:     ) {
19:         let kind = node.kind();
20:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
21: 
22:         if kind == "function_definition" {
23:             // Find the function name node.
24:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
25:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
26:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
27: 
28:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
29:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
30:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
31:                 {
32:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
33:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
34:                         message: format!(
35:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
36:                             name
37:                         ),
38:                         severity: Severity::Error,
39:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
40:                         line: pos.row + 1,
41:                         column: pos.column + 1,
42:                         fix: None,
43:                     });
44:                 }
45: 
46:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
47:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
48:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
49:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",

52:                             name

60:                 }

62:         }

1: //! `check_name_value` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_name_value(
7:         &self,
8:         call: Node,
9:         args: Option<Node>,
10:         source: &str,
11:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
12:     ) {
13:         // Assignment shape: `f('Bad Name' = 1)` parses as an assignment whose
14:         // LHS is a function_call with a MISSING closing paren.
15:         let is_assignment_lhs = call.parent().is_some_and(|p| {
16:             p.kind() == "assignment"
17:                 && p.child_by_field_name("left")
18:                     .is_some_and(|l| l.id() == call.id())
19:         });
20:         let has_missing_paren = (0..call.child_count()).any(|i| {
21:             call.child(i)
22:                 .is_some_and(|c| c.is_missing() && c.kind() == ")")
23:         });
24:         if is_assignment_lhs && has_missing_paren {
25:             if let Some(name) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
26:                 self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
27:             }
28:         }
29: 
30:         // ERROR shape: an ERROR node containing `=` inside the call's args.
31:         for e in Self::call_error_nodes(call) {
32:             let text = &source[e.start_byte()..e.end_byte()];
33:             if !text.contains('=') {
34:                 continue;
35:             }
36:             let name = if Self::has_string_child(e) {
37:                 e
38:             } else if let Some(last) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
39:                 last
40:             } else {
41:                 e
42:             };
43:             self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
44:         }
45: 
46:         // Direct `=` tokens inside arguments (name=value parses cleanly only
47:         // for valid identifier names).
48:         if let Some(a) = args {
49:             for i in 0..a.child_count() {
50:                 if let Some(eq) = a.child(i) {
51:                     if eq.kind() != "=" {
52:                         continue;
53:                     }
54:                     if let Some(name) = eq.prev_named_sibling() {
55:                         self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
56:                     }
57:                 }
58:             }
59:         }
60:     }
61: }

6:     pub(crate) fn check_reserved_and_not(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {

13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         let kind = node.kind();
19: 
20:         if node.is_error() {
21:             let start = node.start_byte();
22:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
23:             let pos = node.start_position();
24:             let text = &source[start..end.min(source.len())];
25: 
26:             // MCPLD: ERROR inside a property declaration in a properties block.
27:             if self.is_check_enabled("MCPLD") && Self::inside_property(node) {
28:                 let name = Self::ancestor_of_kind(node, "property")
29:                     .and_then(|prop| Self::first_child_text(prop, "identifier", source))
30:                     .unwrap_or("(unknown)");

32:                     rule_id: "MCPLD",

34:                     severity: Severity::Error,

36:                     line: pos.row + 1,
37:                     column: pos.column + 1,
38:                     fix: None,

40:             }

45:                     rule_id: "SYNEND",

53:             } else if self.is_check_enabled("RESWD") {

55:                     if kw != "end" {
56:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
57:                             rule_id: "RESWD",
58:                             message: "Invalid use of a reserved word.".to_string(),
59:                             severity: Severity::Error,
60:                             byte_range: start..end,
61:                             line: pos.row + 1,
62:                             column: pos.column + 1,
63:                             fix: None,
64:                         });
65:                     }
66:                 }
67:             }
68: 
69:             // BADNOT: bare `~` statement.
70:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT") && text.trim() == "~" {
71:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
72:                     rule_id: "BADNOT",
73:                     message: "Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context."
74:                         .to_string(),
75:                     severity: Severity::Error,
76:                     byte_range: start..end,
77:                     line: pos.row + 1,
78:                     column: pos.column + 1,
79:                     fix: None,
80:                 });
81:             }
82:         }
83: 
84:         // BADNOT: `~` used as a value operator with a malformed operand.
85:         if kind == "not_operator"
86:             && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT")
87:             && Self::has_error_or_missing_descendant(node)
88:         {
89:             let start = node.start_byte();
90:             let end = node.end_byte();
91:             let pos = node.start_position();

95:                 severity: Severity::Error,

97:                 line: pos.row + 1,
98:                 column: pos.column + 1,
99:                 fix: None,
100:             });
101:         }
102: 
103:         // BADNOTLHS: `~` adjacent to an output variable without a comma.
104:         if kind == "multioutput_variable" && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOTLHS") {
105:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
106:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
107:             for (i, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
108:                 if child.kind() != "ignored_argument" {
109:                     continue;
110:                 }
111:                 let prev_is_id = i > 0 && children[i - 1].kind() == "identifier";
112:                 let next_is_id = i + 1 < children.len() && children[i + 1].kind() == "identifier";
113:                 if prev_is_id || next_is_id {
114:                     let pos = child.start_position();
115:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
116:                             rule_id: "BADNOTLHS",
117:                             message: "Invalid use of logical not operator (~) on left side of an assignment. To use ~ to ignore function outputs, separate output variables with commas."
118:                                 .to_string(),
119:                             severity: Severity::Error,
120:                             byte_range: child.byte_range(),
121:                             line: pos.row + 1,
122:                             column: pos.column + 1,
123:                             fix: None,
124:                         });
125:                 }
126:             }
127:         }
128: 
129:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
130:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
131:             self.walk_reserved_and_not(child, source, diagnostics);
132:         }
133:     }
134: }

1: //! `check_statements` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8: 
9:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
10:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
11:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
12:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
13: 
14:         self.walk_statements(
15:             root,
16:             source,
17:             &mut diagnostics,
18:             &mut function_names,
19:             &mut variable_names,
20:             &mut redef_reported,
21:         );
22: 
23:         diagnostics
24:     }
25: 
26:     pub(crate) fn walk_statements(
27:         &self,
28:         node: Node,
29:         source: &str,
30:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
31:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
32:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
33:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
34:     ) {
35:         let kind = node.kind();
36: 
37:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
38:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
39:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
40:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
41:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
42:                     let pos = node.start_position();
43:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
44:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
45:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
46:                         severity: Severity::Error,
47:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
48:                         line: pos.row + 1,
49:                         column: pos.column + 1,
50:                         fix: None,
51:                     });
52:                 }
53:             }
54:         }
55: 
56:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
57:         if kind == "function_definition" {
58:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
59:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
60:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
61:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
62:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
63:                 {
64:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
65:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
66:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
67:                         message: format!(
68:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
69:                             name
70:                         ),
71:                         severity: Severity::Error,
72:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
73:                         line: pos.row + 1,
74:                         column: pos.column + 1,
75:                         fix: None,
76:                     });
77:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
78:                 }
79:                 function_names.insert(name);
80:             }
81:         }
82: 
83:         if kind == "assignment" {
84:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
85:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
86:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
87:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
88:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
89:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
90:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
91:                     {
92:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
93:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
94:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
95:                             message: format!(
96:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
97:                                 name
98:                             ),
99:                             severity: Severity::Error,
100:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
101:                             line: pos.row + 1,
102:                             column: pos.column + 1,
103:                             fix: None,
104:                         });
105:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
106:                     }
107:                     variable_names.insert(name);
108:                 }
109:             }
110:         }
111: 
112:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
113:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
114:         // on the same line without separator.
115:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
116:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
117:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
118: 
119:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
120:                 let prev = pair[0];
121:                 let curr = pair[1];
122: 
123:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
124:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
125:                     continue;
126:                 }
127:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
128:                     continue;
129:                 }
130: 
131:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
132:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
133:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
134: 
135:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
136:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
137:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
138:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
139:                     if between_start < between_end {
140:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
141:                         let has_separator = between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
142:                         if !has_separator {
143:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
144:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
145:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
146:                                 message: "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
147:                                     .to_string(),
148:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
149:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
150:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
151:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
152:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
153:                             });
154:                         }
155:                     }
156:                 }
157:             }
158:         }
159: 
160:         // Recurse into children.
161:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
162:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
163:             self.walk_statements(
164:                 child,
165:                 source,
166:                 diagnostics,
167:                 function_names,
168:                 variable_names,
169:                 redef_reported,
170:             );
171:         }
172:     }
173: }

1: //! `check_unterminated` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_unterminated(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         let mut reported: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
9: 
10:         if self.is_check_enabled("STRIN") || self.is_check_enabled("DOUQT") {
11:             Self::walk_unterminated_strings(root, source, &mut diagnostics, &mut reported);
12:         }
13: 
14:         if self.is_check_enabled("INBLK") {
15:             Self::walk_unterminated_comments(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
16:         }
17: 
18:         diagnostics
19:     }
20: 
21:     pub(crate) fn walk_unterminated_strings(
22:         node: Node,
23:         source: &str,
24:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
25:         reported: &mut HashSet<usize>,
26:     ) {
27:         if node.is_error() {
28:             // STRIN: ERROR node whose text starts with an unmatched quote.
29:             let start = node.start_byte();
30:             let end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
31:             let text = &source[start..end];
32:             if text.starts_with('\'')
33:                 && text.matches('\'').count() % 2 == 1
34:                 && !reported.contains(&start)
35:                 && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, start)
36:             {
37:                 let pos = node.start_position();
38:                 reported.insert(start);
39:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
40:                     rule_id: "STRIN",
41:                     message: "A quoted character vector is unterminated.".to_string(),
42:                     severity: Severity::Error,
43:                     byte_range: start..start + 1,
44:                     line: pos.row + 1,
45:                     column: pos.column + 1,
46:                     fix: None,
47:                 });
48:             }
49: 
50:             // STRIN/DOUQT: direct quote tokens inside the ERROR node.
51:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
52:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
53:                 if child.kind() == "'" {
54:                     let pos = child.start_byte();
55:                     if !reported.contains(&pos) && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, pos) {
56:                         let cpos = child.start_position();
57:                         reported.insert(pos);
58:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
59:                             rule_id: "STRIN",
60:                             message: "A quoted character vector is unterminated.".to_string(),
61:                             severity: Severity::Error,
62:                             byte_range: pos..pos + 1,
63:                             line: cpos.row + 1,
64:                             column: cpos.column + 1,
65:                             fix: None,
66:                         });
67:                     }
68:                 } else if child.kind() == "\"" {
69:                     let pos = child.start_byte();
70:                     if !reported.contains(&pos) {
71:                         let cpos = child.start_position();
72:                         reported.insert(pos);
73:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
74:                             rule_id: "DOUQT",
75:                             message: "A double quoted string is unterminated.".to_string(),
76:                             severity: Severity::Error,
77:                             byte_range: pos..pos + 1,
78:                             line: cpos.row + 1,
79:                             column: cpos.column + 1,
80:                             fix: None,
81:                         });
82:                     }
83:                 }
84:             }
85:         }
86: 
87:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
88:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
89:             Self::walk_unterminated_strings(child, source, diagnostics, reported);
90:         }
91:     }

93:     pub(crate) fn walk_unterminated_comments(
94:         node: Node,
95:         source: &str,
96:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,

6:     pub(crate) fn check_validation_order(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         if !self.is_check_enabled("VTPOD") {
9:             return diagnostics;

16:         &self,
17:         node: Node,
18:         source: &str,
19:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
20:     ) {
21:         if node.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
22:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
23:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
24:                 if child.kind() == "property" {
25:                     self.check_property_validation_order(child, source, diagnostics);
26:                 }
27:             }
28:         }
29:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
30:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
31:             self.walk_validation_order(child, source, diagnostics);
32:         }
33:     }

35:     pub(crate) fn check_property_validation_order(
36:         &self,
37:         property: Node,
38:         source: &str,
39:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
40:     ) {
41:         let name = property.child_by_field_name("name");
42:         let vf = Self::find_validation_functions(property);
43:         let mut class_id: Option<Node> = None;
44: 
45:         for i in 0..property.child_count() {
46:             let Some(child) = property.child(i) else {
47:                 continue;
48:             };
49:             if child.kind() == "identifier" && Some(child) != name && class_id.is_none() {
50:                 class_id = Some(child);
51:             }
52:         }
53:

55:         if let (Some(class_id), Some(vf)) = (class_id, vf) {
